title: And, the other way around
summary: Build a complete proof that p and q give q and p by assuming, taking apart, rebuilding, and finishing.

blocks.text:
The conjunction p ∧ q says that p and q both hold. From it, we can prove q ∧ p. This is not a new fact about p or q. It follows from the meaning of and.

The proof has four moves. Assume the conjunction. Take it into its two parts. Split the new conjunction into two goals. Close each goal with the part it needs.

blocks.alt: The goal changes from p and q implies q and p to two smaller goals, q and p; hypotheses named hp and hq supply p and q respectively.

blocks.text:
Assume h : p ∧ q. changes the goal to q ∧ p and records h as evidence. By cases on h, as hp and hq. replaces that evidence with hp : p and hq : q.

It suffices to show q and p. then opens two goals, q first and p second. The goals share the available hypotheses, but each needs its own closing step. From hq. closes q. From hp. closes p.

challenge.prompt: Write the full proof that the two sides of a conjunction can change places.
challenge.statement: Theorem and_swap. For all p q, p ∧ q → q ∧ p.
solution: By cases on h, as hp and hq.
It suffices to show q and p.

challenge.prompt: Write the conclusion with q on the left and p on the right. That exact order matters to the kernel here.
hints: Begin with q, then ∧, then p.

challenge.prompt: The two closing steps have changed places. Decide whether the proof still checks.
challenge.statement: Theorem wrong_order. For all p q, p ∧ q → q ∧ p.
